items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: we played together in Paige's orchestra

ctx.x: But I did not worry about that as long as he treated me fairly. He never paid us for the date we did at the park, after he had lost all the money and then winning it back took off for New York leaving us to get back the best way they could. We forgave him and forgot it in a manner.

We played a battle of jazz with Zack White's Orchestra in Cincinnati which had as its Director a young alto player named Tremb but better known as Inky because he was so black. I had met Inky some years before in Richmond, Ky., where he was born. I had gone there with Clarence Page and Helvey. Inky had seen Cecil Scott work and had copied the style of wearing a top hat which Cecil and Fess Williams had copied from Ted Lewis. Zack had a very nice orchestra but we were too much for them because we had been together…
We also washed away the orchestra of Speed Webb in a battle of jazz in Cincinnati. Roy Eldridge and Teddy Wilson were in the band but I did not know Teddy then.
